You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# TTY via pty for stdout only, stderr pipe etc using script? Use pty openpty and subprocess stdout slave stderr slave separately
import subprocess as sp
def run_tty(args, stdout_tty=True, stderr_tty=True, env=None):
    master_out, slave_out = pty.openpty() if stdout_tty else (None,None)
    master_err, slave_err = pty.openpty() if stderr_tty else (None,None)
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    p=sp.Popen([EXE]+args,cwd=d,stdout=slave_out if stdout_tty else sp.PIPE,stderr=slave_err if stderr_tty else sp.PIPE,env=e,text=False)
    if slave_out is not None: os.close(slave_out)
    if slave_err is not None: os.close(slave_err)
    out=b""; err=b""

    p.wait(timeout=5)
    if stdout_tty:
        try:
            while True:
                chunk=os.read(master_out,4096)

    else: out=p.stdout.read() if p.stdout else b""
    if stderr_tty:
        try:
            while True:
                chunk=os.read(master_err,4096)
                if not chunk: break
                err+=chunk
        except OSError: pass
        os.close(master_err)
    else: err=p.stderr.read() if p.stderr else b""

pub mod differ;
pub mod sequencematcher;
mod utils;

use sequencematcher::{Sequence, SequenceMatcher};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt::Display;
use utils::{format_range_context, format_range_unified};

pub fn get_close_matches<'a>(
    word: &str,
    possibilities: Vec<&'a str>,
    n: usize,
    cutoff: f32,
) -> Vec<&'a str> {
    if !(0.0 <= cutoff && cutoff <= 1.0) {
        panic!("Cutoff must be greater than 0.0 and lower than 1.0");
    }
    let mut res: Vec<(f32, &str)> = Vec::new();
    let mut matcher = SequenceMatcher::new("", word);
    for i in &possibilities {
        matcher.set_first_seq(i);
        let ratio = matcher.ratio();
        if ratio >= cutoff {
            res.push((ratio, i));
        }
    }
    res.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap());
    res.truncate(n);
    res.iter().map(|x| x.1).collect()
}

pub fn unified_diff<T: Sequence + Display>(
    first_sequence: &[T],
    second_sequence: &[T],
    from_file: &str,
    to_file: &str,
    from_file_date: &str,
    to_file_date: &str,
    n: usize,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut res = Vec::new();
    let lineterm = '\n';
    let mut started = false;
    let mut matcher = SequenceMatcher::new(first_sequence, second_sequence);
    for group in &matcher.get_grouped_opcodes(n) {
        if !started {
            started = true;

        let file1_range = format_range_unified(first.first_start, last.first_end);

pub fn context_diff<T: Sequence + Display>(
    first_sequence: &[T],
    second_sequence: &[T],
    from_file: &str,
    to_file: &str,
    from_file_date: &str,
    to_file_date: &str,
    n: usize,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut res = Vec::new();
    let lineterm = '\n';
    let mut prefix: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    prefix.insert(String::from("insert"), String::from("+ "));
    prefix.insert(String::from("delete"), String::from("- "));
    prefix.insert(String::from("replace"), String::from("! "));
    prefix.insert(String::from("equal"), String::from("  "));
    let mut started = false;
    let mut matcher = SequenceMatcher::new(first_sequence, second_sequence);
    for group in &matcher.get_grouped_opcodes(n) {
        if !started {
            started = true;
            let from_date = format!("\t{}", from_file_date);
            let to_date = format!("\t{}", to_file_date);
            res.push(format!("*** {}{}{}", from_file, from_date, lineterm));
            res.push(format!("--- {}{}{}", to_file, to_date, lineterm));
        }
        let (first, last) = (group.first().unwrap(), group.last().unwrap());
        res.push(format!("***************{}", lineterm));
        let file1_range = format_range_context(first.first_start, last.first_end);
        res.push(format!("*** {} ****{}", file1_range, lineterm));

                    for item in first_sequence
                        .iter()
                        .take(opcode.first_end)
                        .skip(opcode.first_start)
                    {
                        res.push(format!("{}{}", &prefix[&opcode.tag], item));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        let file2_range = format_range_context(first.second_start, last.second_end);
        res.push(format!("--- {} ----{}", file2_range, lineterm));
        any = false;
        for opcode in group {
            if opcode.tag == "replace" || opcode.tag == "insert" {

    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    for path,content in spec.items():
        p=os.path.join(d,path)
        if content is None:
            os.makedirs(p,exist_ok=True)
        elif isinstance(content,tuple) and content[0]=="link":
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True) if os.path.dirname(path) else None
            os.symlink(content[1],p)
        elif isinstance(content,tuple) and content[0]=="fifo":
            os.mkfifo(p)
        else:
            if os.path.dirname(path): os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True)
            with open(p,"wb") as f: f.write(content if isinstance(content,bytes) else str(content).encode())
    return d
def tree(d):
    out={}
    for root,dirs,files in os.walk(d):
        dirs.sort()
        for name in sorted(dirs+files):
            p=os.path.join(root,name); rel=os.path.relpath(p,d)
            # normalize dump timestamp names
            reln=re.sub(r'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d(_\d{6}| \d\d:\d\d:\d\d)','DATE',rel)
            if os.path.islink(p): out[reln]=("link",os.readlink(p))
            elif os.path.isdir(p): out[reln]=("dir",)
            elif os.path.isfile(p):
                data=open(p,'rb').read()
                try:
                    s=data.decode(); s=re.sub(r'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d','DATE',s); data=s.encode()
                except: pass
                out[reln]=("file",data,oct(os.stat(p).st_mode & 0o777))

        b=subprocess.run([NEW]+args,cwd=d2,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=5)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        print("TIMEOUT",name,e); return False
    # Normalize absolute temp paths if any
    ao=a.stdout.replace(d1,"/TMP"); bo=b.stdout.replace(d2,"/TMP")
    ae=a.stderr.replace(d1,"/TMP"); be=b.stderr.replace(d2,"/TMP")
    # Panic thread ids and locations differ; normalize panic locations for now
    def norm_panic(s):
        s=re.sub(r"thread 'main' \(\d+\) panicked at [^:]+:\d+:\d+:", "thread 'main' panicked:",s)

    ae=norm_panic(ae); be=norm_panic(be)
    # Dump timestamps in stderr (dump create errors)
    ae=re.sub(r'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d_\d{6}','DATE',ae); be=re.sub(r'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d_\d{6}','DATE',be)
    ok=True
    if a.returncode!=b.returncode: ok=False

        if sorted(ao.splitlines())!=sorted(bo.splitlines()): ok=False
    elif ao!=bo: ok=False

    t1=tree(d1);t2=tree(d2)
    # For normalize_order, dump operation order in json may differ; canonicalize dump operation arrays sorting if needed
    if normalize_order:
        def canon(t):
            t=dict(t)
            for k,v in list(t.items()):

                    except Exception: pass
            return t
        t1=canon(t1);t2=canon(t2)
    if t1!=t2: ok=False
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ")+name)

        print(" ref err",repr(ae)); print(" new err",repr(be))
        print(" ref tree",t1); print(" new tree",t2)

/// A fragment of a computed diff.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Result<T> {
    /// An element that only exists in the left input.
    Left(T),
    /// Elements that exist in both inputs.
    Both(T, T),
    /// An element that only exists in the right input.
    Right(T),
}

/// Computes the diff between two slices.
pub fn slice<'a, T: PartialEq>(left: &'a [T], right: &'a [T]) -> Vec<Result<&'a T>> {
    do_diff(left, right, |t| t)
}

/// Computes the diff between the lines of two strings.
pub fn lines<'a>(left: &'a str, right: &'a str) -> Vec<Result<&'a str>> {
    let mut diff = do_diff(
        &left.lines().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        &right.lines().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        |str| *str,
    );
    // str::lines() does not yield an empty str at the end if the str ends with
    // '\n'. We handle this special case by inserting one last diff item,
    // depending on whether the left string ends with '\n', or the right one,
    // or both.
    match (
        left.as_bytes().last().cloned(),
        right.as_bytes().last().cloned(),
    ) {
        (Some(b'\n'), Some(b'\n')) => {
            diff.push(Result::Both(&left[left.len()..], &right[right.len()..]))
        }
        (Some(b'\n'), _) => diff.push(Result::Left(&left[left.len()..])),
        (_, Some(b'\n')) => diff.push(Result::Right(&right[right.len()..])),
        _ => {}
    }
    diff
}

/// Computes the diff between the chars of two strings.
pub fn chars<'a>(left: &'a str, right: &'a str) -> Vec<Result<char>> {
    do_diff(
        &left.chars().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        &right.chars().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        |char| *char,
    )
}

fn do_diff<'a, T, F, U>(left: &'a [T], right: &'a [T], mapper: F) -> Vec<Result<U>>
where
    T: PartialEq,
    F: Fn(&'a T) -> U,
{
    let leading_equals = left
        .iter()
        .zip(right.iter())
        .take_while(|(l, r)| l == r)
        .count();
    let trailing_equals = left[leading_equals..]
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .zip(right[leading_equals..].iter().rev())
        .take_while(|(l, r)| l == r)
        .count();

    let table: Vec2<u32> = {
        let left_diff_size = left.len() - leading_equals - trailing_equals;
        let right_diff_size = right.len() - leading_equals - trailing_equals;

        let mut table = Vec2::new(0, [left_diff_size + 1, right_diff_size + 1]);

        let left_skip = &left[leading_equals..left.len() - trailing_equals];
        let right_skip = &right[leading_equals..right.len() - trailing_equals];

        for (i, l) in left_skip.iter().enumerate() {
            for (j, r) in right_skip.iter().enumerate() {
                table.set(
                    [i + 1, j + 1],
                    if l == r {
                        table.get([i, j]) + 1
                    } else {
                        *table.get([i, j + 1]).max(table.get([i + 1, j]))
                    },
                );
            }
        }

        table
    };

    let mut diff = Vec::with_capacity(left.len().max(right.len()));

    diff.extend(
        left[..leading_equals]
            .iter()
            .zip(&right[..leading_equals])
            .map(|(l, r)| Result::Both(mapper(l), mapper(r))),
    );

    {
        let start = diff.len();
        let mut i = table.len[0] - 1;
        let mut j = table.len[1] - 1;
        let left = &left[leading_equals..];
        let right = &right[leading_equals..];

        loop {
            if j > 0 && (i == 0 || table.get([i, j]) == table.get([i, j - 1])) {
                j -= 1;
                diff.push(Result::Right(mapper(&right[j])));
            } else if i > 0 && (j == 0 || table.get([i, j]) == table.get([i - 1, j])) {
                i -= 1;
                diff.push(Result::Left(mapper(&left[i])));
            } else if i > 0 && j > 0 {
                i -= 1;
                j -= 1;
                diff.push(Result::Both(mapper(&left[i]), mapper(&right[j])));
            } else {
                break;
            }
        }
        diff[start..].reverse();
    }

    diff.extend(
        left[left.len() - trailing_equals..]
            .iter()
            .zip(&right[right.len() - trailing_equals..])
            .map(|(l, r)| Result::Both(mapper(l), mapper(r))),
    );

    diff
}

struct Vec2<T> {
    len: [usize; 2],
    data: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T> Vec2<T> {
    #[inline]
    fn new(value: T, len: [usize; 2]) -> Self
    where
        T: Clone,
    {
        Vec2 {
            len,
            data: vec![value; len[0] * len[1]],
        }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn get(&self, index: [usize; 2]) -> &T {
        debug_assert!(index[0] < self.len[0]);
        debug_assert!(index[1] < self.len[1]);
        &self.data[index[0] * self.len[1] + index[1]]
    }

    #[inline]
    fn set(&mut self, index: [usize; 2], value: T) {
        debug_assert!(index[0] < self.len[0]);
        debug_assert!(index[1] < self.len[1]);
        self.data[index[0] * self.len[1] + index[1]] = value;
    }
}

   else: x=v.get(k-1,0)+1
   y=x-k

   v[k]=x

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    let mut regex_command = Command::new("regex")
        .about("Rename files and directories using a regular expression")
        .arg_required_else_help(true);
    for arg in common_args() {
        regex_command = regex_command.arg(arg);
    }
    regex_command = regex_command
        .arg(
            Arg::new("replace-limit")
                .short('l')
                .long("replace-limit")
                .help("Limit of replacements, all matches if set to 0")
                .value_name("LIMIT")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("replace-transform")
                .short('t')
                .long("replace-transform")
                .help("Apply a transformation to replacements including captured groups")
                .value_name("REPLACE_TRANSFORM")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(ReplaceTransform)),
        );
    for arg in traversal_args() {
        regex_command = regex_command.arg(arg);
    }
    regex_command = regex_command
        .arg(
            Arg::new("expression")
                .help("Expression to match (can be a regex)")
                .required(true)
                .value_name("EXPRESSION"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("replacement")
                .help("Expression replacement (use single quotes for capture groups)")
                .required(true)
                .value_name("REPLACEMENT"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("paths")
                .help("Target paths")
                .required(true)
                .value_name("PATH(S)")
                .num_args(1..),
        );

    let mut from_file_command = Command::new("from-file")
        .about("Read operations from a dump file")
        .arg_required_else_help(true);
    for arg in common_args() {
        from_file_command = from_file_command.arg(arg);
    }
    from_file_command = from_file_command
        .arg(
            Arg::new("undo")
                .short('u')
                .long("undo")
                .help("Undo the operations from the dump file")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("dumpfile")
                .required(true)
                .value_name("DUMPFILE"),
        );

    let mut to_ascii_command = Command::new("to-ascii")
        .about("Replace file name UTF-8 chars with ASCII chars representation")
        .arg_required_else_help(true);
    for arg in common_args() {
        to_ascii_command = to_ascii_command.arg(arg);
    }
    for arg in traversal_args() {
        to_ascii_command = to_ascii_command.arg(arg);
    }
    to_ascii_command = to_ascii_command.arg(
        Arg::new("paths")
            .help("Target paths")
            .required(true)
            .value_name("PATH(S)")
            .num_args(1..),
    );

    Command::new("rnr")
        .version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
        .about("RnR is a command-line tool to rename multiple files and directories that\nsupports regular expressions\n")
        .arg_required_else_help(true)
        .subcommand_required(true)
        .subcommand(regex_command)
        .subcommand(from_file_command)
        .subcommand(to_ascii_command)
}

fn make_renamer(matches: &ArgMatches) -> Renamer {
    let color_value = matches
        .get_one::<ColorMode>("color")
        .copied()
        .unwrap_or(ColorMode::Auto);
    let color_enabled = match color_value {
        ColorMode::Always => true,
        ColorMode::Never => false,
        ColorMode::Auto => std::io::stdout().is_terminal(),
    };
    color::set_enabled(color_enabled);
    Renamer::new(
    Renamer::new(
        matches.get_flag("force"),
        matches.get_flag("backup"),
        matches.get_flag("silent"),
        matches.get_flag("dump"),
        matches
            .get_one::<String>("dump-prefix")
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "rnr-".to_string()),
        matches.get_flag("no-dump"),
    )
}

fn make_traversal(matches: &ArgMatches) -> TraversalOptions {
    TraversalOptions {
        include_dirs: matches.get_flag("include-dirs"),
        recursive: matches.get_flag("recursive"),
        max_depth: matches.get_one::<usize>("max-depth").copied(),
        hidden: matches.get_flag("hidden"),
    }
}

fn get_paths(matches: &ArgMatches) -> Vec<String> {
    matches
        .get_many::<String>("paths")
        .map(|values| values.cloned().collect())
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

fn run_regex(matches: &ArgMatches) -> AppResult<()> {
    let renamer = make_renamer(matches);
    let transform = matches.get_one::<ReplaceTransform>("replace-transform").copied();
    let solver = RegexSolver::new(
        matches.get_one::<String>("expression").unwrap(),
        matches.get_one::<String>("replacement").unwrap().clone(),
        matches.get_one::<usize>("replace-limit").copied(),
        transform,
        make_traversal(matches),
        get_paths(matches),
    )?;
    renamer.rename_with_regex(&solver)
}

fn run_from_file(matches: &ArgMatches) -> AppResult<()> {
    let renamer = make_renamer(matches);
    renamer.rename_from_file(
        matches.get_one::<String>("dumpfile").unwrap(),
        matches.get_flag("undo"),
    )
}

fn run_to_ascii(matches: &ArgMatches) -> AppResult<()> {
    let renamer = make_renamer(matches);
    let solver = AsciiSolver::new(make_traversal(matches), get_paths(matches));
    renamer.rename_to_ascii(&solver)
}

fn main() {
    let matches = build_cli().get_matches();
    let (result, silent) = match matches.subcommand() {
        Some(("regex", submatches)) => (run_regex(submatches), submatches.get_flag("silent")),
        Some(("from-file", submatches)) => {
            (run_from_file(submatches), submatches.get_flag("silent"))
        }
        Some(("to-ascii", submatches)) => {
            (run_to_ascii(submatches), submatches.get_flag("silent"))
        }
        _ => (Ok(()), false),
    };
    if let Err(error) = result {
        let is_bad_expression = matches!(error, errors::AppError::BadExpression(_));
        if is_bad_expression && silent {
            color::set_enabled(false);
        }
        if !silent || is_bad_expression {
            eprintln!("{}{}", color::red("Error: "), error);
        }
        process::exit(1);
    }
}

use crate::ascii;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ReplaceTransform {
    Upper,
    Lower,
    Ascii,
}

impl clap::ValueEnum for ReplaceTransform {
    fn value_variants<'a>() -> &'a [Self] {
        &[Self::Upper, Self::Lower, Self::Ascii]
    }

    fn to_possible_value(&self) -> Option<clap::builder::PossibleValue> {
        Some(clap::builder::PossibleValue::new(match self {
            Self::Upper => "upper",
            Self::Lower => "lower",
            Self::Ascii => "ascii",
        }))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TraversalOptions {
    pub include_dirs: bool,
    pub recursive: bool,
    pub max_depth: Option<usize>,
    pub hidden: bool,
}

fn is_hidden(entry: &DirEntry) -> bool {
    entry.depth() > 0
        && entry
            .file_name()
            .to_str()
            .map(fileutils::is_hidden_name)
            .unwrap_or(false)
}

pub fn solve_paths(paths: &[String], options: &TraversalOptions) -> HashSet<PathBuf> {
    let mut solved = HashSet::new();
    for path in paths.iter().map(PathBuf::from) {
        if options.recursive {
            let mut builder = WalkDir::new(&path);
            if let Some(max_depth) = options.max_depth {
                builder = builder.max_depth(max_depth);
            }
            let walker = builder.into_iter().filter_entry(|entry| {
                options.hidden || !is_hidden(entry)
            });
            for entry in walker {
                if let Ok(entry) = entry {
                    let entry_path = entry.into_path();
                    if entry_path.to_str().is_none() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if !options.include_dirs && entry_path.is_dir() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    solved.insert(entry_path);
                }
            }
        } else {
            if !fileutils::path_exists(&path) {
                continue;
            }
            if !options.include_dirs && path.is_dir() {
                continue;
            }
            solved.insert(path);
        }
    }
    solved
}

fn build_operations<F>(paths: &[String], options: &TraversalOptions, mut rename: F) -> AppResult<Operations>
where
    F: FnMut(&str) -> String,
{
    let mut operations = Vec::new();
    for path in solve_paths(paths, options) {
        let Some(file_name) = path.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) else {
            continue;
        };
        let new_file_name = rename(file_name);
        if new_file_name != file_name {
            operations.push(Operation {
                target: fileutils::with_file_name(&path, &new_file_name),
                source: path,
            });
        }
    }
    let mut operations = Operations::new(operations);
    operations.check_duplicate_targets()?;
    operations.sort_by_depth();
    operations.check_existing_targets()?;
    Ok(operations)
}

        replacement: String,
        limit: Option<usize>,
        transform: Option<ReplaceTransform>,
        traversal: TraversalOptions,
        paths: Vec<String>,
    ) -> AppResult<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            regex: Regex::new(expression).map_err(AppError::BadExpression)?,
            replacement,
            limit: limit.unwrap_or(1),
            transform,
            traversal,
            paths,
        })
    }

    pub fn get_operations(&self) -> AppResult<Operations> {
        build_operations(&self.paths, &self.traversal, |file_name| {
            match self.transform {
                None => self
                    .regex
                    .replacen(file_name, self.limit, self.replacement.as_str())
                    .into_owned(),
                Some(transform) => self
                    .regex
                    .replacen(file_name, self.limit, |captures: &Captures<'_>| {
                        let mut expanded = String::new();
                        captures.expand(&self.replacement, &mut expanded);
                        match transform {
                            ReplaceTransform::Upper => expanded.to_uppercase(),
                            ReplaceTransform::Lower => expanded.to_lowercase(),
                            ReplaceTransform::Ascii => ascii::to_ascii(&expanded),
                        }
                    })
                    .into_owned(),
            }
        })
    }
}

pub struct AsciiSolver {
    traversal: TraversalOptions,
    paths: Vec<String>,
}

impl AsciiSolver {
    pub fn new(traversal: TraversalOptions, paths: Vec<String>) -> Self {
        Self { traversal, paths }
    }

    pub fn get_operations(&self) -> AppResult<Operations> {
        build_operations(&self.paths, &self.traversal, ascii::to_ascii)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Operations {
    pub date: String,
    pub operations: Vec<Operation>,
}

impl Operations {
    pub fn new(operations: Vec<Operation>) -> Self {
        Self {
            date: String::new(),
            operations,
        }
    }

    pub fn from_file(path: &str) -> AppResult<Self> {
        let path_buf = PathBuf::from(path);
        let file = File::open(path)
            .map_err(|_| AppError::CannotOpenReadFile(path_buf.clone()))?;
        serde_json::from_reader(file)
            .map_err(|_| AppError::CannotParseJsonFile(path_buf))
    }

    pub fn dump(&mut self, prefix: &str) -> AppResult<()> {
        let now = Local::now();
        let file_name = format!("{}{}.json", prefix, now.format("%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S"));
        let file_path = PathBuf::from(&file_name);
        let file = File::create(&file_name)
            .map_err(|_| AppError::CannotCreateFile(file_path.clone()))?;
        self.date = now.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S").to_string();
        serde_json::to_writer_pretty(file, self)
            .map_err(|_| AppError::CannotParseJsonFile(file_path))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn check_duplicate_targets(&self) -> AppResult<()> {
        let mut first_by_target: HashMap<&PathBuf, &Operation> = HashMap::new();
        let mut collisions = String::new();
        let mut sorted: Vec<&Operation> = self.operations.iter().collect();
        sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.source.cmp(&b.source));
        for operation in sorted {
            if let Some(first) = first_by_target.get(&operation.target) {
                collisions.push_str(&color::red(&format!(
                    "\n{}->{}\n{}->{}\n",
                    first.source.display(),
                    first.target.display(),
                    operation.source.display(),
                    operation.target.display()
                )));
            } else {
                first_by_target.insert(&operation.target, operation);
            }
        }
        if collisions.is_empty() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(AppError::FilesWithSameName(collisions))
        }
    }

    pub fn sort_by_depth(&mut self) {
        self.operations.sort_by(|a, b| {
            fileutils::component_count(&b.target)
                .cmp(&fileutils::component_count(&a.target))
        });
    }

    pub fn check_existing_targets(&self) -> AppResult<()> {
        let sources: HashSet<&PathBuf> = self.operations.iter().map(|op| &op.source).collect();
        for operation in &self.operations {
            if !sources.contains(&operation.target)
                && fileutils::path_exists(&operation.target)
            {
                return Err(AppError::ConflictWithExistingPath(
                    operation.source.clone(),
                    operation.target.clone(),
                ));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

pub enum AppError {

impl fmt::Display for AppError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {

                )
            }
            AppError::CannotCreateBackup(path) => {
                write!(

                    "Cannot create a backup of {}",

                )
            }
            AppError::CannotRename(source, target, e) => {

                )
            }
            AppError::FilesWithSameName(collisions) => {
                write!(f, "Files will have the same name\n{}", color::red(collisions))
            }
        }
    }
}

use crate::ascii_data;

fn hangul_to_ascii(c: char) -> Option<String> {
    let code = c as u32;
    if !(0xAC00..=0xD7A3).contains(&code) {
        return None;
    }
    const INITIAL: [&str; 19] = [
        "g", "kk", "n", "d", "tt", "l", "m", "b", "pp", "s", "ss", "", "j", "jj", "ch", "k",
        "t", "p", "h",
    ];
    const MEDIAL: [&str; 21] = [
        "a", "ae", "ya", "yae", "eo", "e", "yeo", "ye", "o", "wa", "wae", "oe", "yo", "u",
        "wo", "we", "wi", "yu", "eu", "ui", "i",
    ];
    const FINAL: [&str; 28] = [
        "", "g", "kk", "gs", "n", "nj", "nh", "d", "l", "lg", "lm", "lb", "ls", "lt", "lp",
        "lh", "m", "b", "bs", "s", "ss", "ng", "j", "ch", "k", "t", "p", "h",
    ];
    let offset = code - 0xAC00;
    let mut result = String::new();
    result.push_str(INITIAL[(offset / 588) as usize]);
    result.push_str(MEDIAL[((offset % 588) / 28) as usize]);
    result.push_str(FINAL[(offset % 28) as usize]);
    let mut chars = result.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => Some(first.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() + chars.as_str()),
        None => Some(result),
    }
}

fn char_to_ascii(c: char) -> Option<String> {
    let code = c as u32;
    if (0xE0020..=0xE007E).contains(&code) {
        return char::from_u32(code - 0xE0000).map(|mapped| mapped.to_string());
    }
    if let Some(mapped) = ascii_data::lookup(c) {
        return Some(mapped.to_string());
    }
    hangul_to_ascii(c)
}

pub fn to_ascii(input: &str) -> String {
    if input.is_ascii() {
        return input.to_string();
    }
    let mut result = String::with_capacity(input.len());
    for c in input.chars() {
        if c.is_ascii() {
            result.push(c);
        } else if let Some(mapped) = char_to_ascii(c) {
            result.push_str(&mapped);
        }
    }
    result
}
